headline: Histology and spot data decoded into single-cell RNA and protein profiles
label: Histology To Spatial Omics Inference
summary: H&E foundation models and generative predictors (GeneFlow, SCOPE, Loki2, GenVinci) extend histology-to-omics inference to large panels and single cells.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring molecular state from cheaper or coarser modalities. GeneFlow uses flow matching with histology and gene tokenizers to predict panels of up to 1,000 spatial genes. SCOPE predicts single-cell RNA and protein from H&E using RNA-protein biomarker priors across 16 organs. Loki2, a single-cell pathology foundation model trained on 15M cells, recovers transcriptomic and protein signals from H&E. GenVinci, trained on a 300M-profile corpus, reconstructs 3D tissue from histology to map senescence. sc-HistoMorphomics links 194 nuclear features to spatial transcriptomics. A related strand raises resolution within spatial data: st2sc infers single-cell expression from multicellular spots, SpOTr couples Fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport with deconvolution, and a rotation-equivariant model reconstructs 3D cell shape from transcript point clouds to improve protein prediction. Flow matching also appears in ST-FateFlow for time-resolved spatial dynamics. Clustering, metacell, and gene-selection methods form a separate background.
